newsitem.title: USA: NYSE nominates Panetta, Komansky for board.
newsitem.headline: NYSE nominates Panetta, Komansky for board.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said on Wednesday its nominating committee named Leon Panetta, former chief of staff for President Bill Clinton and a former congressman, as a candidate for the NYSE board.
Also nominated was David Komansky, president and chief executive of Merrill Lynch and Co Inc.
Panetta would replace Anthony O'Reilly, the chairman and chief executive of H.J. Heinz Co, who has served three consecutive terms, the maximum permitted.
Komansky would replace Stephen Hammerman, chairman of Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Smith Inc, who is retiring from the exchange board.
Ten current directors were nominated for re-election:

The incumbent public directors nominated were Paul Allaire, chairman and chief executive of Xerox Corp ; Geoffrey Bible, chairman and chief executive of Philip Morris Cos Inc ; J. Gary Burkhead, president and chief executive of Fidelity Management and Research Co; Bernard Marcus, chairman and chief executive of Home Depot Inc ; and Kathryn Whitmire, director of the National Resource Center for Public Leadership at the University of Maryland.

The securities industries directors nominated were Charles Bocklet Jr, managing partner, Bocklet & Co LP; Michel David-Weill, chairman of Lazard Freres & Co LLC; Robert Fagenson, president of Fagenson & Co Inc; Richard Fisher, chairman of Morgan Stanley Group Inc ; and Benjamin Griswold IV, chairman of Alex. Brown & Sons Inc.
